text: The inhabitants of Obtahete are a study, well-made, active, and comedy people. The statture of the men in general, is from five feet seven to five feet ten inches the tallest man seen by Captain Wallis measured six feet three inches and a half, said Captain Cook, in his second wynge, describes OTos, the king of Obtahets to be of that height. "In order to paint a Hercules or in Mary," says M. de Bougainville, "one could nowhere find much beautiful models." They see if a given brown completers in general their hair is black, and finely frizzed j they have black eyes, flat noises, large mouths, and fine white teeth y. He men wear their laarde in many fashions, all of them plocking out a great part, and have prominent bellies. Most of them smell strong of the coconut oil. The women in general are much smaller, especially those of the lower rank or tawtows, which is attributed to their early and promotions intercourse with the men i), whilst the better sort who do not grafify their passion in the same unbriched manner, are above the middle stature of Expensans. Their skin is most definitely smooth and soft: they have in color in their checks i; their nose is generally somewhat flat, but their eyes are full of expression, and their teeth beautifully even and white. "The women," says M. de Bougainville, "have features not less agreeable than the generality of Europens, and a symmetry of body and beautiful proportion of links which might vie with any of them.
